outcome.summary: For k=4 and k=5, a random k-SAT formula on n variables with ⌊a_k n⌋ independent clauses (each on k distinct, uniformly chosen variables with independent fair signs) is unsatisfiable with probability tending to one. Here a_4 = 249/25 = 9.96 and a_5 = 1057/50 = 21.14. Explicitly, P[SAT] ≤ exp(−n/31,872,000,000) for n ≥ 254,976,000,000 when k=4, and P[SAT] ≤ exp(−n/422,800,000,000) for n ≥ 3,382,400,000,000 when k=5. By monotonicity the same holds at every larger density. The proof extends to general k the integer-cost, y-reweighted energetic interpolation of Vorobyev (arXiv:2610.10599, k=3). Positivity comes from the nonnegative degree-k remainder (Lelarge–Oulamara), so it holds for odd k. The proof was checked line by line by a referee but is not formally verified or externally refereed. Th
